payload.answer:
IBM How to use the LIKE operator, wildcard and special characters in your IBM FileNet Content Platform Engine Sweep's Filter Expression - United States

TECHNOTE (FAQ)

QUESTION
 How to use the LIKE operator, wildcard and special characters in your IBM FileNet Content Platform Engine Sweep's Filter Expression? 

CAUSE
A sweep is an instance of a background service that you configure to process objects in a database table or some other set of items. To optimize sweep performance, you can optionally make the filter expression for the sweep a part of the WHERE clause of the sweep query. This inclusion means that the sweep retrieves only those database rows that satisfy the filter conditions.
The criteria is expressed in terms of properties and values of the objects that are targeted by the sweep. The syntax is a subset of the SQL syntax for the WHERE clause. [S1]

1. Log into IBM FileNet Application Console for Content Platform Engine (ACCE).
2. Go to your object store => Sweep Management => Sweep Policies => Disposal Policies.
3. Create a new disposal policy with the following criteria.
- Sweep mode = normal
- Target class = Recovery Item
Go to Data Design => Other Classes => Recover Item, right click and 'Copy object reference'.
- Filter expression = Now() > DateCreated + TimeSpan(90, 'days')
TimeSpan can use the following units: seconds, minutes, hours & days.
- Effective start date and Effective end date
Type in the fields something like 'July 1 2016' and hit the tab key. It will put in the value as something like 'July 1, 2016 at 12:00:00 AM Pacific Standard Time'

The solution to this problem is to delete the Sweep Result records in one or more separate operations prior to deleting the parent Job Sweep. There are two possible approaches to this solution. The first is to simply use ACCE to delete the Sweep Result objects manually. This can be accomplished by navigating to the Sweep Result tab for the Sweep Job object that you want to delete and selecting a subset of the Sweep Result objects and clicking on the Delete button. Repeat this process until all the Sweep Result objects have been deleted or until a sufficient number has been deleted to allow the parent Job Sweep to be deleted without exceeding the transaction time-out limit.

The TIMELIMIT value of the query is set to the value of the FilteredQueryTimeout property (TIMELIMIT 90). The time limit is applied only to the first query of the sweep iteration. If the query time limit is exceeded, then the query terminates and the sweep falls back to using a query that does not contain the filter expression in the WHERE clause. The sweep continues to use the WHERE clause without the filter expression until the iteration is completed. If the query time limit is not exceeded during the first query, then the sweep continues to use the WHERE clause with the filter expression until the sweep iteration is completed.

Setting the FilteredQueryTimeout value
You can use the Content Platform Engine administration console to set the FilteredQueryTimeout value for existing job and policy sweeps.
